# minimaxflash-1.3 — the player's own report was lost

> **This file is not the player's report.** The player wrote one, at
> `runs/minimaxflash-1.3/REPORT.md`, after it had already run `archive` — so
> the archive never contained it — and another session then overwrote the file
> with a reconstruction. `runs/` is not in git, so there is no copy. The
> account that run wrote about itself is gone, and this note stands where it
> was rather than letting a reconstruction read as the record.
>
> That is also why both prompts now say to write the report **before** running
> the finishing commands: the order they gave put `archive` first.

What survives of this run, in its own words, is its notebook:
[knowledge/minimaxflash-1.3.md](../../knowledge/minimaxflash-1.3.md), 26
promoted lines of what it found, and its own commit message:

> *minimaxflash-1.3: depth 1, level 4, alive; found the cursor-and-g
> exploration walk, no down staircase*

What the record says: 610 asks, 4,219 keypresses, turn 17,281, High-Elf Druid,
depth 2, character level 4, alive. The third life of this character, carried
on from `minimaxflash-1-again`.

The one thing worth drawing from it, which its commit message states and its
notebook supports: **the first life of this character wrote itself a 143-line
breadth-first search and never tried the game's own pathfinding; that failure
became a note; the note was moved to the top of `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md`; and
this life used `lxg`.** It still found no down staircase, which is the honest
limit of that tip — `lxg` explores, and `l>g` needs a staircase already on the
map.
